Bacterial isolate taxonomy from SILVA ACT classification

  • Show All Code
  • Hide All Code
  • View Source
Author

Shane Hogle

Published

October 7, 2026

Abstract
Parses SILVA ACT classifications of the consensus 16S sequences assembled in 01_sanger_seq/01_trace_qc_assembly.qmd, builds a per-isolate taxonomy table, and summarizes genus/family/phylum composition and phylogeny.

The consensus 16S sequences produced in 01.A Trace QC + assembly were submitted to the SILVA ACT web aligner with LCA classification against SILVA SSU and GTDB enabled. This notebook reads back the two downloaded ACT outputs — the classification result list and the guide tree — and joins them to the per-isolate assembly metadata to build the taxonomy table and summary figures.

1 Setup

1.1 Libraries

Loads required libraries

Show/hide code 
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(fs)
library(ape)
library(treeio)
library(ggtree)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(Polychrome)
library(DT)
library(taxplore)

source(here::here("R", "plotting.R"))

1.2 Global variables

Show/hide code 
data_raw <- here::here(
  "data",
  "raw",
  "sanger_sequencing",
  "20261006_arb_silva_cat"
)
data_processed_sanger <- here::here("data", "processed", "01_sanger_seq")
data_processed <- here::here("data", "processed", "02_bac_taxonomy")

fs::dir_create(data_processed)

silva_resultlist <- here::here(
  data_raw,
  "arb-silva.de_align_resultlist_1512869.csv"
)
silva_tree_file <- here::here(
  data_raw,
  "arb-silva.de_2026-10-06_id1512869.tree"
)

outgroup_genus <- "Lactococcus"

2 Read and parse SILVA ACT output

SILVA SSU lineage strings are semicolon-delimited as Domain;<unnamed>;Phylum;Class;Order;Family;Genus, with the second field always empty, and ambiguous LCA nodes suffixed with --other. GTDB lineage strings instead carry g__/s__ prefixed tokens. The two helpers below pull out the ranks we need from each scheme.

Show/hide code 
parse_silva_taxonomy <- function(tax_string) {
  ranks <- c("domain", "phylum", "class", "order", "family", "genus")
  rank_idx <- c(1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7)
  empty <- c("None", "Unclassified;", "")

  if (is.na(tax_string) || tax_string %in% empty) {
    return(
      set_names(as.list(rep(NA_character_, length(ranks))), ranks) |>
        as_tibble()
    )
  }

  parts <- tax_string |>
    str_remove(";$") |>
    str_split(";") |>
    pluck(1) |>
    str_trim()
  parts <- parts[parts != ""]
  parts <- str_remove(parts, "--other")

  vals <- map_chr(
    rank_idx,
    ~ if (length(parts) >= .x) parts[.x] else NA_character_
  )
  set_names(as.list(vals), ranks) |> as_tibble()
}

parse_gtdb_taxonomy <- function(tax_string) {
  empty <- c("None", "Unclassified;", "")
  if (is.na(tax_string) || tax_string %in% empty) {
    return(tibble(gtdb_genus = NA_character_, gtdb_species = NA_character_))
  }

  parts <- tax_string |>
    str_remove(";$") |>
    str_split(";") |>
    pluck(1) |>
    str_trim()
  parts <- parts[parts != ""]

  tibble(
    gtdb_genus = parts |>
      str_subset("^g__") |>
      str_remove("^g__") |>
      pluck(1, .default = NA_character_),
    gtdb_species = parts |>
      str_subset("^s__") |>
      str_remove("^s__") |>
      pluck(1, .default = NA_character_)
  )
}

Read the result list and apply the parsers row-wise

Show/hide code 
silva_raw <- read_delim(
  silva_resultlist,
  delim = ";",
  quote = '"',
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

silva_tax <- silva_raw$lca_tax_slv |> map_dfr(parse_silva_taxonomy)
gtdb_tax <- silva_raw$lca_tax_gtdb |> map_dfr(parse_gtdb_taxonomy)

silva_parsed <- silva_raw |>
  select(
    seq_id = sequence_identifier,
    silva_identity = identity,
    silva_quality = quality,
    silva_score = sequence_score
  ) |>
  bind_cols(silva_tax, gtdb_tax)

3 Build taxonomy table

Join the SILVA classification onto the per-isolate assembly metadata from the trace QC/assembly step

Show/hide code 
assemblies <- read_csv(
  here::here(data_processed_sanger, "assemblies.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  filter(sample_key != "negative control")

taxonomy_table <- assemblies |>
  select(
    seq_id,
    batch,
    sample_key,
    strain_id = strainID,
    bacteria_plate_well = isolation_plate_well,
    location = isolation_loc,
    google_drive_id,
    assembly_type,
    consensus_length,
    fwd_trimmed_length,
    rev_trimmed_length,
    overlap_length,
    overlap_mismatches,
    fwd_rev_overlap_identity = overlap_pct_identity,
    alignment_score
  ) |>
  left_join(silva_parsed, by = "seq_id")

4 Define representative strains

For isolates with more than one run of sequencing (e.g., HA01 has HA01_20250605_25FALAA000, HA01_20250905_2657LAA000, and HA01_20260529_EC00233196) define a representative 16S rRNA assembly as the assembly with

  1. fewest overlap_mismatches
  2. highest overlap_pct_identity
  3. highest alignment_score

The best-ranked assembly of each multi-run strain is flagged as the representative. Strains whose sequencing runs disagree in SILVA genus or GTDB family and order assignment are flagged

Show/hide code 
taxonomy_table_rep <- taxonomy_table |>
  group_by(sample_key) |>
  arrange(
    desc(alignment_score),
    desc(fwd_rev_overlap_identity),
    overlap_mismatches,
    .by_group = TRUE
  ) |>
  mutate(
    n_seq_runs = n(),
    is_representative = row_number() == 1L
  ) |>
  ungroup()

# strains whose runs disagree in SILVA genus or GTDB species assignment
tax_disagreement <- taxonomy_table_rep |>
  group_by(sample_key) |>
  summarise(
    across(c(order, family), ~ n_distinct(na.omit(.x)) > 1L),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  rename(
    order_disagreement = order,
    family_disagreement = family
  ) |>
  mutate(
    strain_has_disagreement = order_disagreement | family_disagreement
  )

taxonomy_table_rep_dis <- taxonomy_table_rep |>
  left_join(tax_disagreement, by = "sample_key")

write_csv(
  taxonomy_table_rep_dis,
  here::here(data_processed, "isolate_taxonomy_table.csv")
)

Table displaying summary discordant taxonomic assignments of different isolates

Table displaying detailed discordant taxonomic assignments of different isolates and all their Sanger sequencing batches

Some basic taxonomy summaries

5 Final results

Only isolates with a resolved SILVA SSU classification (domain not missing) are used below. We also return the representative sequence only.

Show/hide code 
classified <- taxonomy_table_rep_dis |>
  filter(!is.na(domain)) |>
  filter(is_representative)

write_csv(
  classified,
  here::here(data_processed, "representative_isolate_taxonomy_table.csv")
)

6 Taxonomy figures

The panels below summarize isolate composition and phylogeny.

6.1 Krona plots

6.2 Genus composition across all isolates

A shared palette for phylum, plus a helper that bins a taxonomic rank into its top categories (grouping everything else as "Other") and computes relative composition per sampling site. Plot styling (theme_project(), capit()) and the make_palette() generator live in R/plotting.R, shared with other notebooks in this project.

Show/hide code 
phylum_colors <- c(
  "Pseudomonadota" = "#1f78b4",
  "Bacteroidota" = "#ff7f00",
  "Bacillota" = "#33a02c",
  "Deinococcota" = "#e31a1c"
)

composition_by_site <- function(
  df,
  rank_col,
  top_n,
  palette,
  other_color = "grey60"
) {
  top_cats <- df |>
    filter(!is.na(.data[[rank_col]])) |>
    count(.data[[rank_col]], sort = TRUE) |>
    slice_head(n = top_n) |>
    pull(1)

  plot_df <- df |>
    filter(!is.na(location)) |>
    mutate(
      cat = if_else(.data[[rank_col]] %in% top_cats, .data[[rank_col]], "Other")
    ) |>
    count(location, cat) |>
    group_by(location) |>
    mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n)) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(cat = factor(cat, levels = c(top_cats, "Other")))

  cat_colors <- c(palette[top_cats], "Other" = other_color)

  ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = location, y = pct, fill = cat)) +
    geom_col(color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = cat_colors, name = str_to_title(rank_col)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "% of isolates") +
    capit() +
    theme_project() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "right",
      legend.title = element_text(),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1)
    )
}
Show/hide code 
genus_counts <- classified |> count(genus, sort = TRUE)

top_genus <- genus_counts |> filter(!is.na(genus)) |> slice_head(n = 12)
other_n <- genus_counts |>
  filter(!genus %in% top_genus$genus | is.na(genus)) |>
  summarise(n = sum(n)) |>
  pull(n)

genus_plot_df <- bind_rows(top_genus, tibble(genus = "Other", n = other_n)) |>
  mutate(genus = fct_reorder(genus, n))
Show/hide code 
ggplot(genus_plot_df, aes(x = n, y = genus)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#1f78b4") +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), hjust = -0.3, size = 3) +
  labs(x = "Number of isolates", y = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  capit() +
  theme_project()

6.7 Phylogeny

The SILVA ACT guide tree for this job contains only our isolates (no SILVA reference sequences). For the phylogeny below we root the tree on an isolate classified as Lactococcus (Bacillota, the most basal phylum recovered).

Show/hide code 
tree <- ape::read.tree(silva_tree_file)

outgroup_tip <- classified |>
  filter(genus == outgroup_genus, seq_id %in% tree$tip.label) |>
  pull(seq_id) |>
  pluck(1)

tree_rooted <- ape::root(tree, outgroup = outgroup_tip, resolve.root = TRUE)

isolate_tips <- intersect(tree_rooted$tip.label, classified$seq_id)
tree_pruned <- ape::keep.tip(tree_rooted, isolate_tips)

Every family recovered among the tree’s isolates gets its own tip color below — nothing is pooled into an “Other” category. Isolates with a domain-level SILVA classification but no resolved family are labeled “Unclassified”.

Show/hide code 
all_family_tree <- classified |>
  filter(seq_id %in% isolate_tips, !is.na(family)) |>
  distinct(family) |>
  arrange(family) |>
  pull(family)

family_tree_pal <- make_palette(all_family_tree)

tip_data <- assemblies |>
  filter(seq_id %in% isolate_tips) |>
  select(seq_id) |>
  left_join(
    classified |> select(seq_id, family),
    by = "seq_id"
  ) |>
  transmute(
    label = seq_id,
    seq_id,
    family_grp = coalesce(family, "Unclassified")
  )
Show/hide code 
ggtree(tree_pruned, layout = "rectangular") %<+%
  tip_data +
  geom_tippoint(aes(color = family_grp), size = 1.5) +
  geom_tiplab(aes(label = seq_id), size = 2, hjust = -0.1) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(family_tree_pal, "Unclassified" = "grey50"),
    name = "Family"
  ) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(ncol = 1, override.aes = list(size = 3))) +
  geom_treescale(offset = 1)

# Read and parse SILVA ACT output

SILVA SSU lineage strings are semicolon-delimited as `Domain;<unnamed>;Phylum;Class;Order;Family;Genus`, with the second field always empty, and ambiguous LCA nodes suffixed with `--other`. GTDB lineage strings instead carry `g__`/`s__` prefixed tokens. The two helpers below pull out the ranks we need from each scheme.

```{r}
parse_silva_taxonomy <- function(tax_string) {
  ranks <- c("domain", "phylum", "class", "order", "family", "genus")
  rank_idx <- c(1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7)
  empty <- c("None", "Unclassified;", "")

  if (is.na(tax_string) || tax_string %in% empty) {
    return(
      set_names(as.list(rep(NA_character_, length(ranks))), ranks) |>
        as_tibble()
    )
  }

  parts <- tax_string |>
    str_remove(";$") |>
    str_split(";") |>
    pluck(1) |>
    str_trim()
  parts <- parts[parts != ""]
  parts <- str_remove(parts, "--other")

  vals <- map_chr(
    rank_idx,
    ~ if (length(parts) >= .x) parts[.x] else NA_character_
  )
  set_names(as.list(vals), ranks) |> as_tibble()
}

parse_gtdb_taxonomy <- function(tax_string) {
  empty <- c("None", "Unclassified;", "")
  if (is.na(tax_string) || tax_string %in% empty) {
    return(tibble(gtdb_genus = NA_character_, gtdb_species = NA_character_))
  }

  parts <- tax_string |>
    str_remove(";$") |>
    str_split(";") |>
    pluck(1) |>
    str_trim()
  parts <- parts[parts != ""]

  tibble(
    gtdb_genus = parts |>
      str_subset("^g__") |>
      str_remove("^g__") |>
      pluck(1, .default = NA_character_),
    gtdb_species = parts |>
      str_subset("^s__") |>
      str_remove("^s__") |>
      pluck(1, .default = NA_character_)
  )
}
```

Read the result list and apply the parsers row-wise
```{r}
silva_raw <- read_delim(
  silva_resultlist,
  delim = ";",
  quote = '"',
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

silva_tax <- silva_raw$lca_tax_slv |> map_dfr(parse_silva_taxonomy)
gtdb_tax <- silva_raw$lca_tax_gtdb |> map_dfr(parse_gtdb_taxonomy)

silva_parsed <- silva_raw |>
  select(
    seq_id = sequence_identifier,
    silva_identity = identity,
    silva_quality = quality,
    silva_score = sequence_score
  ) |>
  bind_cols(silva_tax, gtdb_tax)
```

# Build taxonomy table

Join the SILVA classification onto the per-isolate assembly metadata from the trace QC/assembly step

```{r}
assemblies <- read_csv(
  here::here(data_processed_sanger, "assemblies.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  filter(sample_key != "negative control")

taxonomy_table <- assemblies |>
  select(
    seq_id,
    batch,
    sample_key,
    strain_id = strainID,
    bacteria_plate_well = isolation_plate_well,
    location = isolation_loc,
    google_drive_id,
    assembly_type,
    consensus_length,
    fwd_trimmed_length,
    rev_trimmed_length,
    overlap_length,
    overlap_mismatches,
    fwd_rev_overlap_identity = overlap_pct_identity,
    alignment_score
  ) |>
  left_join(silva_parsed, by = "seq_id")
```

# Define representative strains

For isolates with more than one run of sequencing (e.g., `HA01` has `HA01_20250605_25FALAA000`, `HA01_20250905_2657LAA000`, and `HA01_20260529_EC00233196`) define a representative 16S rRNA assembly as the assembly with

1. fewest `overlap_mismatches`
2. highest `overlap_pct_identity`
3. highest `alignment_score`

The best-ranked assembly of each multi-run strain is flagged as the representative. Strains whose sequencing runs disagree in SILVA genus or GTDB family and order assignment are flagged

```{r}
taxonomy_table_rep <- taxonomy_table |>
  group_by(sample_key) |>
  arrange(
    desc(alignment_score),
    desc(fwd_rev_overlap_identity),
    overlap_mismatches,
    .by_group = TRUE
  ) |>
  mutate(
    n_seq_runs = n(),
    is_representative = row_number() == 1L
  ) |>
  ungroup()

# strains whose runs disagree in SILVA genus or GTDB species assignment
tax_disagreement <- taxonomy_table_rep |>
  group_by(sample_key) |>
  summarise(
    across(c(order, family), ~ n_distinct(na.omit(.x)) > 1L),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  rename(
    order_disagreement = order,
    family_disagreement = family
  ) |>
  mutate(
    strain_has_disagreement = order_disagreement | family_disagreement
  )

taxonomy_table_rep_dis <- taxonomy_table_rep |>
  left_join(tax_disagreement, by = "sample_key")

write_csv(
  taxonomy_table_rep_dis,
  here::here(data_processed, "isolate_taxonomy_table.csv")
)
```

```{r}
#| output: true
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: Table displaying summary discordant taxonomic assignments of different isolates
tibble(
  metric = c(
    "strains",
    "strains with multiple sequencing runs",
    "strains flagged: Order disagreement",
    "strains flagged: Family disagreement"
  ),
  value = c(
    n_distinct(taxonomy_table_rep_dis$strain_id),
    sum(
      taxonomy_table_rep_dis$n_seq_runs > 1 &
        taxonomy_table_rep_dis$is_representative
    ),
    sum(taxonomy_table_rep_dis$order_disagreement),
    sum(taxonomy_table_rep_dis$family_disagreement)
  )
)
```

```{r}
#| output: true
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: Table displaying detailed discordant taxonomic assignments of different isolates and all their Sanger sequencing batches
taxonomy_table_rep_dis |>
  filter(strain_has_disagreement) |>
  dplyr::select(
    sample_key,
    alignment_score,
    silva_quality,
    silva_score,
    overlap_mismatches,
    fwd_rev_overlap_identity,
    seq_id,
    order,
    family
  ) |>
  arrange(sample_key) |>
  DT::datatable(
    class = "cell-border stripe",
    rownames = FALSE,
    extensions = "FixedColumns",
    caption = "Sequencing runs of strains with discordant taxonomic assignments",
    options = list(
      dom = "ft",
      pageLength = -1,
      scrollX = TRUE,
      fixedColumns = TRUE
    )
  )
```


```{r}
#| output: true
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: Some basic taxonomy summaries

n_genus <- sum(!is.na(taxonomy_table_rep_dis$genus))
n_genera <- n_distinct(na.omit(taxonomy_table_rep_dis$genus))
n_unclassified <- sum(is.na(taxonomy_table_rep_dis$domain))
n_gtdb_species <- sum(!is.na(taxonomy_table_rep_dis$gtdb_species))

tibble(
  metric = c(
    "isolates",
    "genus-level calls",
    "distinct genera",
    "unclassified",
    "GTDB species calls"
  ),
  value = c(
    nrow(taxonomy_table_rep_dis),
    n_genus,
    n_genera,
    n_unclassified,
    n_gtdb_species
  )
)
```

# Final results

Only isolates with a resolved SILVA SSU classification (`domain` not missing) are used below. We also return the representative sequence only.

```{r}
classified <- taxonomy_table_rep_dis |>
  filter(!is.na(domain)) |>
  filter(is_representative)

write_csv(
  classified,
  here::here(data_processed, "representative_isolate_taxonomy_table.csv")
)
```

```{r}
  DT::datatable(
    class = "cell-border stripe",
    rownames = FALSE,
    extensions = "FixedColumns",
    options = list(
      dom = "ft",
      pageLength = -1,
      scrollX = TRUE,
      fixedColumns = TRUE
    )
  )
```

## Genus composition across all isolates

A shared palette for phylum, plus a helper that bins a taxonomic rank into its top categories (grouping everything else as `"Other"`) and computes relative composition per sampling site. Plot styling (`theme_project()`, `capit()`) and the `make_palette()` generator live in [`R/plotting.R`](../../R/plotting.R), shared with other notebooks in this project.

```{r}
phylum_colors <- c(
  "Pseudomonadota" = "#1f78b4",
  "Bacteroidota" = "#ff7f00",
  "Bacillota" = "#33a02c",
  "Deinococcota" = "#e31a1c"
)

composition_by_site <- function(
  df,
  rank_col,
  top_n,
  palette,
  other_color = "grey60"
) {
  top_cats <- df |>
    filter(!is.na(.data[[rank_col]])) |>
    count(.data[[rank_col]], sort = TRUE) |>
    slice_head(n = top_n) |>
    pull(1)

  plot_df <- df |>
    filter(!is.na(location)) |>
    mutate(
      cat = if_else(.data[[rank_col]] %in% top_cats, .data[[rank_col]], "Other")
    ) |>
    count(location, cat) |>
    group_by(location) |>
    mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n)) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(cat = factor(cat, levels = c(top_cats, "Other")))

  cat_colors <- c(palette[top_cats], "Other" = other_color)

  ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = location, y = pct, fill = cat)) +
    geom_col(color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = cat_colors, name = str_to_title(rank_col)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "% of isolates") +
    capit() +
    theme_project() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "right",
      legend.title = element_text(),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1)
    )
}
```

```{r}
genus_counts <- classified |> count(genus, sort = TRUE)

top_genus <- genus_counts |> filter(!is.na(genus)) |> slice_head(n = 12)
other_n <- genus_counts |>
  filter(!genus %in% top_genus$genus | is.na(genus)) |>
  summarise(n = sum(n)) |>
  pull(n)

genus_plot_df <- bind_rows(top_genus, tibble(genus = "Other", n = other_n)) |>
  mutate(genus = fct_reorder(genus, n))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-genus-counts
#| output: true
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("Genus composition across all ", nrow(classified), ' classified isolates. The 12 most abundant genera are shown individually; all remaining genera are pooled as "Other".')
ggplot(genus_plot_df, aes(x = n, y = genus)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#1f78b4") +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), hjust = -0.3, size = 3) +
  labs(x = "Number of isolates", y = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  capit() +
  theme_project()
```

## Phylogeny

The SILVA ACT guide tree for this job contains only our isolates (no SILVA reference sequences). For the phylogeny below we root the tree on an isolate classified as *Lactococcus* (Bacillota, the most basal phylum recovered).

```{r}
tree <- ape::read.tree(silva_tree_file)

outgroup_tip <- classified |>
  filter(genus == outgroup_genus, seq_id %in% tree$tip.label) |>
  pull(seq_id) |>
  pluck(1)

tree_rooted <- ape::root(tree, outgroup = outgroup_tip, resolve.root = TRUE)

isolate_tips <- intersect(tree_rooted$tip.label, classified$seq_id)
tree_pruned <- ape::keep.tip(tree_rooted, isolate_tips)
```

Every family recovered among the tree's isolates gets its own tip color below — nothing is pooled into an "Other" category. Isolates with a domain-level SILVA classification but no resolved family are labeled "Unclassified".

```{r}
all_family_tree <- classified |>
  filter(seq_id %in% isolate_tips, !is.na(family)) |>
  distinct(family) |>
  arrange(family) |>
  pull(family)

family_tree_pal <- make_palette(all_family_tree)

tip_data <- assemblies |>
  filter(seq_id %in% isolate_tips) |>
  select(seq_id) |>
  left_join(
    classified |> select(seq_id, family),
    by = "seq_id"
  ) |>
  transmute(
    label = seq_id,
    seq_id,
    family_grp = coalesce(family, "Unclassified")
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-tree
#| output: true
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 22
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("Phylogeny of the ", length(isolate_tips), " classified isolates, rooted on an isolate classified as *Lactococcus*. Tip points are colored by family, with every family recovered (", length(all_family_tree), ') shown individually; isolates with a domain-level SILVA classification but no resolved family are labeled "Unclassified". Scale bar represents substitutions per site.')
ggtree(tree_pruned, layout = "rectangular") %<+%
  tip_data +
  geom_tippoint(aes(color = family_grp), size = 1.5) +
  geom_tiplab(aes(label = seq_id), size = 2, hjust = -0.1) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(family_tree_pal, "Unclassified" = "grey50"),
    name = "Family"
  ) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(ncol = 1, override.aes = list(size = 3))) +
  geom_treescale(offset = 1)
```
